hook: A declassified USCENTCOM Mission Report documenting an incidental UAP sighting by a U.S. Air Force special operations ISR aircraft during a 20-hour surveillance mission over Greece in January 2024, in which a diamond-shaped object traveling at approximately 434 knots was observed exclusively through a Short-Wave Infrared (SWIR) sensor for roughly two minutes.
why_it_matters: This report is significant because the UAP was detectable only on the SWIR camera and produced no radar return when interrogated, suggesting either a very low radar cross-section or an unusual thermal signature profile — a combination that complicates conventional identification. The structured MISREP format captures the sighting in official DoD reporting channels under USCENTCOM and was explicitly approved for release to AARO, placing it within the formal UAP disclosure pipeline established after the 2022 NDAA. The observer's description of a non-maneuvering probe or 'tail' appended to a diamond shape adds an unusual morphological detail not commonly described in other released UAP reports.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was only detectable through the aircraft's Short-Wave Infrared (SWIR) sensor and did not appear visually or on any other sensor system, with its signature logged as 'SWIR WHT' (white on SWIR).

key_findings.finding: The observer described the UAP as having a round diamond shape with a straight, non-maneuvering appendage extending from the bottom, described alternately as a 'probe' and a 'tail' in different sections of the same report.

key_findings.finding: The UAP was traveling at approximately 434 knots at FL200 (20,000 feet), roughly 5,000 feet below the observing aircraft at FL250, moving on a westward trajectory, while exhibiting altitude variations but no change in heading.

key_findings.finding: The UAP sighting was incidental to the primary mission: the aircraft was conducting ISR surveillance under USCENTCOM tasking, including a vehicle stop-follow operation in which a large white box was observed being transferred between vehicles.

key_findings.finding: Despite unknown propulsion and unknown intelligent control status, the observer formally assessed the UAP as 'Benign,' and the report records no effects on personnel, equipment, or the aircraft, with the two-minute event ending without incident.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' and carries a USCENTCOM MDR reference number, placing it directly within the formal AARO UAP reporting and disclosure chain.
The document is classified SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY throughout, indicating it was authorized for sharing with Five Eyes partner nations at the time of classification.
